title: Okta Domain 3 questions (3.1, 3.2)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with Okta.

questions.stem: An admin needs to store each employee's cost center on their Okta profile. Where should the attribute be added?
choices: Directory > Profile Editor, in the Okta default user profile
Applications > the HR app > Sign On tab attribute statements
Security > Authenticators > Profile settings
Directory > Groups > the Finance group profile
questions.answer: Directory > Profile Editor, in the Okta default user profile
questions.explanation: Custom user attributes are added to the Okta user profile in the Profile Editor. Attribute statements only send values in a SAML assertion and do not create a profile attribute.

questions.stem: A new custom attribute will hold a short text code such as CC-Sales. Which data type should the admin choose?
choices: boolean
integer
string
number
questions.answer: string
questions.explanation: Text values use the string type. Integer and number only accept numeric values, and boolean only true or false.

questions.stem: Each user may hold several certifications, and all of them must be stored in one attribute. Which data type fits BEST?
choices: string
string array
boolean
integer
questions.answer: string array
questions.explanation: An array type holds multiple values in one attribute. A plain string holds a single value.

questions.stem: Users should see their employee number on their Okta profile but not be able to change it. Which attribute setting should the admin use?
choices: User permission set to Hide
Attribute marked as Required
Attribute type changed to boolean with a default
User permission set to Read Only
questions.answer: User permission set to Read Only
questions.explanation: Read Only lets users view the value without editing it. Hide removes it from the user's view entirely.

questions.stem: After creating a custom attribute, which property can the admin no longer change?
choices: Display name
Description
User permission
Variable name
questions.answer: Variable name
questions.explanation: The variable name is how the attribute is referenced in mappings and expressions, so it is fixed after creation. Display name and description stay editable.

questions.stem: An admin is cleaning up the Okta user profile. Which attribute can be deleted from it?
choices: The base login attribute
A custom attribute the admin created earlier
The base email attribute
The base firstName attribute, if no app maps it
questions.answer: A custom attribute the admin created earlier
questions.explanation: Base attributes are part of every Okta user profile and cannot be removed. Custom attributes can be deleted.

questions.stem: A Region attribute must only accept the values North, South, East or West. How should the admin define it?
choices: Define an enumerated list of values for the attribute
Make the attribute required and change its type to integer
Set the attribute's user permission to Hide
Create a group rule for each allowed region
questions.answer: Define an enumerated list of values for the attribute
questions.explanation: An enumerated list restricts the attribute to the listed values. Making it required only forces some value to be present.

questions.stem: What is an app user profile in the Okta Profile Editor?
choices: The Okta user profile shared by every app in the org
The list of authenticators that a user has enrolled for use with one app
The attributes Okta keeps for the user's account in one app
The admin role a user holds for one app integration
questions.answer: The attributes Okta keeps for the user's account in one app
questions.explanation: Each app integration has its own user profile describing the account in that app. The Okta user profile is the central profile that mappings read from.

questions.stem: An admin wants to see which attributes an app integration accepts for its users, such as its role field. Where should the admin look?
choices: The Okta default user profile in the Profile Editor
The app's Sign On tab under credentials details
The app's user profile in the Profile Editor
The app's Push Groups tab
questions.answer: The app's user profile in the Profile Editor
questions.explanation: The Profile Editor lists each app's user profile and its attributes. The Okta default profile only holds Okta's own attributes.

questions.stem: An app attribute must hold a value set separately for each person and never be taken from a group assignment. How should the attribute's scope be set?
choices: User personal
Group
Read Only
Required
questions.answer: User personal
questions.explanation: User personal scope keeps the value per user so group assignment values do not apply. Read Only and Required are separate attribute settings, not scopes.

questions.stem: When assigning an app to a group, the admin fills in a License type field in the assignment dialog. What happens to that value?
choices: It is written to each member's Okta user profile as a custom attribute
It replaces the app's SAML attribute statements
It is ignored until the admin runs an import
It is applied to the app profile of each group member
questions.answer: It is applied to the app profile of each group member
questions.explanation: Values entered at group assignment populate the app user profile for the group's members. They are not written back to the Okta user profile.

questions.stem: In an Okta-to-app mapping, which profile receives the mapped values?
choices: The Okta user profile
The app user profile
The group profile
The admin's profile
questions.answer: The app user profile
questions.explanation: Okta-to-app mappings read the Okta user profile and write to the app user profile, which provisioning then sends to the app.

questions.stem: An admin needs to check the value of one app attribute for a single assigned user. What is the quickest place to look?
choices: Open the mapping Preview tab for a random user
Edit that user's assignment on the app's Assignments tab
Search the System Log for the attribute name
Open the Okta default user profile in the Profile Editor and search
questions.answer: Edit that user's assignment on the app's Assignments tab
questions.explanation: The user's app assignment shows their app user profile values. The Profile Editor shows attribute definitions, not one user's values.

questions.stem: A company runs two instances of the same OIN app for two subsidiaries. How are their app user profiles handled?
choices: Both instances share one app user profile
Only the first instance gets an app user profile
Their attributes merge into the Okta user profile under one app name
Each instance has its own app user profile and mappings
questions.answer: Each instance has its own app user profile and mappings
questions.explanation: Every app instance has a separate app user profile, so mappings can differ per subsidiary. They do not share or merge profiles.

questions.stem: An admin wants the Okta title attribute sent to an app's jobTitle field. Which mapping should the admin edit?
choices: The app to Okta User
The group attribute statement
Okta User to the app
The Okta default profile source
questions.answer: Okta User to the app
questions.explanation: Values flowing from Okta into the app are set in the Okta User to app mapping. The app to Okta User direction brings data from the app into Okta.

questions.stem: An HR app is the trusted source of department data, and Okta should receive those values. Which mapping direction applies?
choices: The HR app to Okta User
Okta User to the HR app
Okta User to every downstream app
Group to Okta User
questions.answer: The HR app to Okta User
questions.explanation: Importing values from an app into Okta uses the app to Okta User mapping. The Okta User to app direction pushes Okta's values out.

questions.stem: An app's username should be calculated from Okta when the account is created, and later Okta profile changes must not recalculate it. Which apply option fits?
choices: Apply mapping on user create only
Apply mapping on user create and update
Do not apply the mapping at all
Apply the mapping only during group push
questions.answer: Apply mapping on user create only
questions.explanation: Create only calculates the value once, at account creation, so later Okta profile changes do not recalculate it. Create and update would recalculate it every time the source attribute changes.

questions.stem: An app must always reflect the user's current manager from Okta. Which apply option should the admin choose for the mapping?
choices: Apply mapping on user create only
Apply the mapping only on deactivation
Apply mapping on user create and update
Apply the mapping only during import
questions.answer: Apply mapping on user create and update
questions.explanation: Create and update pushes the value at creation and again whenever it changes. Create only would leave the manager stale after the first push.

questions.stem: Before saving a new mapping expression, the admin wants to see the result for a real user. What should the admin use?
choices: The System Log with an eventType filter
The Preview tab on the mappings page
The Test API Credentials button
The app's Sign On tab preview
questions.answer: The Preview tab on the mappings page
questions.explanation: The mapping Preview shows what the expression produces for a chosen user. Test API Credentials only checks the API connection.

questions.stem: After saving changes to a mapping, the admin wants existing users' app profiles updated right away. Which option should the admin choose?
choices: Push Groups now
Clear user sessions
Reset the mapping
Apply updates now
questions.answer: Apply updates now
questions.explanation: Okta offers to apply updated mappings to existing users when the mapping is saved. Pushing groups and clearing sessions do not recalculate attributes.

questions.stem: A mapping from Okta title to an app is set to create and update, but a title change never reaches the app. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The app's SAML signing certificate expired and was not yet replaced
The user has not enrolled in Okta Verify
The app's Default RelayState is empty
Update User Attributes is not enabled on the Provisioning tab
questions.answer: Update User Attributes is not enabled on the Provisioning tab
questions.explanation: Mappings calculate the value, but provisioning must have Update User Attributes on to send it. Certificates and RelayState only affect SSO.

questions.stem: Which expression returns the part of a user's email address before the @ sign?
choices: String.substringAfter(user.email, "@")
String.substringBefore(user.email, "@")
String.toUpperCase(user.email)
user.email + "@"
questions.answer: String.substringBefore(user.email, "@")
questions.explanation: substringBefore returns the text before the given separator. substringAfter would return the domain instead.

questions.stem: An app needs a displayName such as Jane Smith built from Okta attributes. Which expression is correct?
choices: user.firstName + " " + user.lastName
user.firstName - user.lastName
String.join(user.lastName)
appuser.firstName + appuser.lastName
questions.answer: user.firstName + " " + user.lastName
questions.explanation: The + operator joins strings, and the quoted space separates the names. appuser refers to the app profile, not the Okta profile, in an Okta-to-app mapping.

questions.stem: An app requires last names in capital letters. Which expression should the admin map?
choices: String.toLowerCase(user.lastName)
String.substringBefore(user.lastName, " ")
String.toUpperCase(user.lastName)
user.lastName + "UPPER"
questions.answer: String.toUpperCase(user.lastName)
questions.explanation: toUpperCase converts the value to capitals. toLowerCase does the opposite.

questions.stem: In an app to Okta User mapping, how does an expression refer to an attribute from the app user profile?
choices: user.attributeName
group.attributeName
appuser.attributeName
org.attributeName
questions.answer: appuser.attributeName
questions.explanation: The app profile is referenced as appuser in app-to-Okta mappings. user refers to the Okta user profile.

questions.stem: In an Okta User to app mapping, how does an expression refer to the Okta user's department?
choices: user.department
appuser.department
source.department
profile.department
questions.answer: user.department
questions.explanation: Okta user attributes are referenced with the user prefix. appuser refers to the app profile being written to.

questions.stem: Users in the Sales department should get the role sales_rep in an app, and everyone else standard. Which expression does this?
choices: user.department = "Sales" + "sales_rep" + "standard"
String.substringBefore(user.department, "sales_rep")
user.department != "Sales" ? "sales_rep" : "standard"
user.department == "Sales" ? "sales_rep" : "standard"
questions.answer: user.department == "Sales" ? "sales_rep" : "standard"
questions.explanation: The conditional (ternary) operator returns the first value when the test is true and the second otherwise. The != option reverses the logic.

questions.stem: An app treats usernames as case sensitive and expects them in lower case. Which expression should be mapped to the app username?
choices: String.toUpperCase(user.login)
String.toLowerCase(user.login)
String.substringAfter(user.login, "@")
user.login + ".lower"
questions.answer: String.toLowerCase(user.login)
questions.explanation: toLowerCase normalizes the login to lower case. substringAfter would return only the domain.

questions.stem: An HR system should master user profiles and lifecycle in Okta. What should the admin enable in that app's To Okta settings?
choices: Enable Create Users for the HR app
Allow the HR app to source Okta users
Enable Sync Password for the HR app
Push the Everyone group to the HR app
questions.answer: Allow the HR app to source Okta users
questions.explanation: Profile sourcing makes the app the master of the users it imports. Create Users pushes accounts out of Okta, the opposite direction.

questions.stem: An admin tries to edit a user's title in Okta, but the field cannot be changed. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: The user is in Password expired status
The user has not enrolled in Okta Verify
The title attribute's user permission is set to Hide for end users
The attribute is sourced from Active Directory or an HR app
questions.answer: The attribute is sourced from Active Directory or an HR app
questions.explanation: Attributes mastered by a profile source are read-only in Okta. Password status and authenticators do not lock profile fields.

questions.stem: Users can come from both Active Directory and an HR app. Where does the admin set which system wins for a user who exists in both?
choices: Directory > Groups, by ranking the groups
Security > Authentication Policies, by ordering the policy rules
Directory > Profile Sources, by ordering the sources
Applications > Assignments, by group priority
questions.answer: Directory > Profile Sources, by ordering the sources
questions.explanation: Profile Sources lists the sourcing apps in priority order. Group priority on an app only resolves conflicting app attribute values.

questions.stem: Users are sourced from Active Directory, but their mobile phone number should be maintained in Okta. What should the admin configure?
choices: Set that attribute's source priority to Inherit from Okta
Remove the users from the Active Directory integration
Make the attribute Read Only for end users
Map the attribute in the Okta User to AD direction only
questions.answer: Set that attribute's source priority to Inherit from Okta
questions.explanation: Attribute-level sourcing lets one attribute be mastered by Okta while the rest still come from AD. Removing users from AD would break their whole sourcing.

questions.stem: Users created directly in the Okta Admin Console have no other profile source. Which system masters their profile?
choices: Okta
Active Directory
The first app they are assigned
The HR app with the highest priority
questions.answer: Okta
questions.explanation: Users created in Okta are Okta-sourced, so Okta is their master. Only imported users can be mastered by another system.

questions.stem: A user's department is sourced from Active Directory and is wrong. How should the admin fix it permanently?
choices: Change it in Okta; the new value will be written back to Active Directory
Change it in Okta and set the attribute to Read Only
Correct it in Active Directory and let the next import update Okta
Delete the user in Okta and import them again
questions.answer: Correct it in Active Directory and let the next import update Okta
questions.explanation: The source system wins, so the change belongs in AD and flows to Okta at the next import. An edit in Okta is blocked or overwritten.

questions.stem: What is the main effect of making an app a profile source for the users it imports?
choices: The app receives every change made in Okta
The app masters their profile attributes and lifecycle
The app becomes the only authenticator the users can sign in with
The app is hidden from users' dashboards
questions.answer: The app masters their profile attributes and lifecycle
questions.explanation: A profile source controls the users' attributes and can drive their status. It does not change authentication or dashboards.

questions.stem: An admin must add a cost center attribute and send it to an app. Put the steps in order.
items: Open Directory > Profile Editor and select the Okta user profile
Add a custom string attribute named costCenter
Open the app's mappings in the Okta User to app direction
Map user.costCenter to the app attribute and check it in Preview
Save the mapping and apply updates to existing users
questions.explanation: The Okta attribute must exist before it can be mapped, and Preview checks the result before saving. Applying updates pushes the value to existing users.

questions.stem: Match each expression to the value it returns for a user named Jane Smith with email jane.smith@example.com.
questions.explanation: substringBefore and substringAfter split at the separator, + joins strings and toUpperCase capitalizes. A lower-case smith would need toLowerCase.

questions.stem: A change to a user's title in Okta must reach an app automatically. Which TWO settings are needed?
choices: An Okta User to app mapping set to create and update
Update User Attributes enabled under To App
An app to Okta User mapping for title
Group Push enabled for the user's group
The attribute's user permission set to Read Only
answers: An Okta User to app mapping set to create and update
Update User Attributes enabled under To App
questions.explanation: The mapping must apply on update and provisioning must be allowed to send updates. An app-to-Okta mapping goes the wrong direction.

questions.stem: An admin creates a user without activating them, so no email is sent and the user cannot sign in yet. What status does the user have?
choices: Pending user action
Active
Suspended
Staged
questions.answer: Staged
questions.explanation: Users created but not yet activated are Staged. Pending user action means activation was sent and the user has not completed it.

questions.stem: A user received an activation email but has not clicked the link or set a password. What status does the Admin Console show?
choices: Staged
Password reset
Locked out
Pending user action
questions.answer: Pending user action
questions.explanation: After activation is sent and before the user completes it, the status is Pending user action. Staged is before activation starts.

questions.stem: An admin resets a user's password from the Admin Console and the user has not yet finished the reset. What is the user's status?
choices: Password expired
Password reset
Pending user action
Deactivated
questions.answer: Password reset
questions.explanation: An admin-initiated reset puts the account in Password reset until the user completes it. Password expired results from an expiry, not a reset request.

questions.stem: A user enters a wrong password more times than the password policy allows. What status does the account move to?
choices: Locked out
Suspended
Password expired
Deactivated
questions.answer: Locked out
questions.explanation: Exceeding the lockout threshold sets the account to Locked out. Suspended is only set when an admin suspends the user.

questions.stem: An admin selects Expire password on a user. What happens at the user's next sign-in?
choices: They are blocked until an admin unlocks the account for them
They receive a new activation email to start over
They must change their password before going further
They lose all app assignments until reassigned
questions.answer: They must change their password before going further
questions.explanation: Expiring the password sets Password expired, so the user must choose a new one at sign-in. Unlocking applies to Locked out accounts.

questions.stem: A contractor starts in two weeks. The admin wants the account ready now but no email sent and no sign-in possible until day one. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Create and activate the user, then suspend until day one
Create and activate the user, then deactivate the account until day one
Create the user without activation, then activate on day one
Create the user and expire the password until day one
questions.answer: Create the user without activation, then activate on day one
questions.explanation: A Staged user exists with no activation email and cannot sign in until the admin activates them. Suspending or deactivating requires activating the account first, which normally sends the activation email.

questions.stem: A user is Locked out after repeated failed attempts, but their password is not compromised. How should the admin restore access with the least disruption?
choices: Unlock the user
Reset the user's password
Deactivate and reactivate the user
Clear the user's sessions
questions.answer: Unlock the user
questions.explanation: Unlock returns the account to Active with the same password. A reset forces a new password the user does not need.

questions.stem: An employee is going on a three-month leave. They must not sign in, but their app assignments should be untouched for their return. What should the admin do?
choices: Deactivate the user
Delete the user
Expire the user's password
Suspend the user
questions.answer: Suspend the user
questions.explanation: Suspension blocks sign-in while leaving app assignments unaffected. Deactivation removes all app assignments.

questions.stem: An employee was terminated today and must lose access to Okta and all assigned apps. Which action fits BEST?
choices: Suspend the user
Deactivate the user
Expire the user's password
Clear the user's sessions only
questions.answer: Deactivate the user
questions.explanation: Deactivation removes app assignments, deletes the password and blocks sign-in, which is the offboarding action. Suspension keeps the assignments in place.

questions.stem: An admin wants to permanently remove an Active user's account from Okta. What must happen first?
choices: The user must be suspended
The user must be deactivated
The user's password must be expired
The user must be moved to Staged
questions.answer: The user must be deactivated
questions.explanation: Okta only allows deleting users that are already deactivated. Suspending does not make a user deletable.

questions.stem: What is a key difference between a suspended user and a deactivated user?
choices: Deactivated users keep app assignments; suspended users lose them
Suspended users can still sign in to the End-User Dashboard
Deactivated users can still be edited and then signed in
Suspended users keep app assignments; deactivated users lose them
questions.answer: Suspended users keep app assignments; deactivated users lose them
questions.explanation: Suspension is temporary and leaves assignments alone; deactivation removes all assignments and the password. Neither status allows sign-in.

questions.stem: A suspended employee returns from leave. What should the admin do to restore their access?
choices: Reactivate the user
Reset the user's authenticators
Unsuspend the user
Create a new account for the user
questions.answer: Unsuspend the user
questions.explanation: Unsuspending returns the user to Active with their assignments intact. Reactivation is the action for deactivated users.

questions.stem: Which user status is required before an admin can suspend an account?
choices: Active
Staged
Deactivated
Pending user action
questions.answer: Active
questions.explanation: Only Active users can be suspended. Staged or pending users have not been activated, and deactivated users are already blocked.

questions.stem: A former employee is rehired. Their old Okta account is still in Deactivated status. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Reactivate the existing account and then confirm their app access
Create a second account with a slightly different username for the rehire
Delete the old account and import the user from a CSV file
Unsuspend the old account so its assignments come back
questions.answer: Reactivate the existing account and then confirm their app access
questions.explanation: Reactivating the existing account avoids duplicate identities; since deactivation removed app assignments, access must be checked afterwards. Unsuspend applies only to suspended users.

questions.stem: A user is deactivated in Okta. Their account in a provisioned app is also disabled. Which feature made this happen?
choices: Update User Attributes under To App
Profile sourcing under To Okta
Deactivate Users under To App
Group Push for the user's group
questions.answer: Deactivate Users under To App
questions.explanation: Deactivate Users deprovisions the app account when the Okta user is deactivated or unassigned. Update User Attributes only changes attribute values.

questions.stem: A user is removed from the only group that assigns them a provisioned app with Deactivate Users enabled. What happens to the app account?
choices: It stays active until the user is also deactivated in Okta
It is deactivated because the user lost the assignment
It is deleted from Okta but stays active in the app
It is moved to a suspended group in the app
questions.answer: It is deactivated because the user lost the assignment
questions.explanation: Losing the group means losing the assignment, which triggers deprovisioning. The user does not need to be deactivated in Okta for this.

questions.stem: A user is suspended in Okta. What happens to their accounts in provisioned apps?
choices: Every app account is deactivated in the apps through provisioning
Every app account is deleted from the apps
Every app password is reset to a random value
Nothing changes in the apps; only Okta sign-in is blocked
questions.answer: Nothing changes in the apps; only Okta sign-in is blocked
questions.explanation: Suspension leaves app assignments untouched, so no deprovisioning is sent. Deactivation is what removes assignments and triggers it.

questions.stem: A SAML-only app has no provisioning. A user is deactivated in Okta. What is true about their account in the app?
choices: Okta deletes the app account through the SAML connection at next sign-in
The app account is deactivated by the SAML certificate
The app account is suspended until the user is deleted
The app account still exists and must be handled in the app
questions.answer: The app account still exists and must be handled in the app
questions.explanation: SAML only handles sign-in, so Okta stops issuing assertions but cannot change the account. The account must be disabled in the app or by another process.

questions.stem: Before offboarding a user, an admin wants a list of every app they have so non-provisioned apps can be handled manually. Where is this found?
choices: The Profile Editor's list of app user profiles
The Applications tab on the user's profile page
The global session policy rules list
The Push Groups tab of each app
questions.answer: The Applications tab on the user's profile page
questions.explanation: The user's Applications tab lists all their assigned apps. The Profile Editor lists app profiles for the org, not one user's apps.

questions.stem: A departing employee used an SWA app where they set their own username and password, and the app has no provisioning. What else should the admin do after deactivating them in Okta?
choices: Disable the account or change its password inside the app
Nothing, because SWA deletes the app account on deactivation
Push the user's group to the app to remove them
Clear the user's sessions so the app password stops working
questions.answer: Disable the account or change its password inside the app
questions.explanation: The user knows the app password and could sign in directly, so the app account must be disabled there. Okta sessions do not affect a password known to the user.

questions.stem: After deactivating a user, how can an admin confirm the action in the System Log?
choices: Filter with eventType eq "user.session.start"
Filter with eventType eq "user.lifecycle.suspend"
Filter with eventType eq "user.lifecycle.deactivate"
Filter with eventType eq "policy.evaluate_sign_on"
questions.answer: Filter with eventType eq "user.lifecycle.deactivate"
questions.explanation: The user.lifecycle.deactivate event records the deactivation; user.lifecycle.suspend records a suspension instead. user.session.start records sign-ins, not lifecycle changes.

questions.stem: A user was deactivated in Okta, yet an hour later they are still working inside a SAML app opened earlier. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: Deactivation only takes effect after 24 hours
The user's Okta Verify enrollment keeps them signed in
The app has its own session that has not expired yet
The deactivation was undone by the next group rule run
questions.answer: The app has its own session that has not expired yet
questions.explanation: Okta controls new sign-ins, but an app's own session lasts until it expires or the account is disabled in the app. Deactivation in Okta is immediate.

questions.stem: An admin wants to end every current Okta session of a user immediately, forcing a new sign-in. What should the admin use?
choices: Clear user sessions on the user's profile
Expire password on the user's profile
Reset authenticators on the user's profile
Unlock on the user's profile
questions.answer: Clear user sessions on the user's profile
questions.explanation: Clear user sessions ends their existing Okta sessions. Expiring the password changes what happens at the next sign-in but is not meant to end sessions.

questions.stem: An admin needs to show that a deactivated user can no longer reach an app. Which check is BEST?
choices: Look at the app's attribute statements on the Sign On tab
Open the Profile Editor and check the app's mappings
Review the authenticator enrollment policy for the user
Attempt a sign-in as the user, then check the System Log
questions.answer: Attempt a sign-in as the user, then check the System Log
questions.explanation: A failed sign-in attempt plus the System Log record proves the user is blocked. Mappings and enrollment policies say nothing about whether access was removed.

questions.stem: An admin wants a list of every user currently deactivated in the org. What is the quickest way?
choices: Search the Profile Editor for deactivated attributes
Filter Directory > People by the Deactivated status
Open the Everyone group and sort by name
Check each app's Assignments tab
questions.answer: Filter Directory > People by the Deactivated status
questions.explanation: The People page can be filtered by user status. Deactivated users have no app assignments to find on the Assignments tab.

questions.stem: After a user's deactivation, the admin wants to confirm their account in a provisioned app was disabled. Which check is BEST?
choices: Confirm the user's tile is missing from the admin's own End-User Dashboard
Look for the deprovisioning event in the System Log and check the app
Open the mapping Preview tab for the user
Check that the user's group still exists in the app
questions.answer: Look for the deprovisioning event in the System Log and check the app
questions.explanation: The System Log shows the provisioning call and the app's console confirms the account state. The mapping Preview only shows attribute calculations.

questions.stem: Users are sourced from Active Directory. When an account is disabled in AD, it should be deactivated in Okta. Which setting achieves this?
choices: Enable Deactivate Users under To App for AD
Create a group rule that removes disabled users
Set the AD option for deactivated users to Do nothing
Set the AD option for deactivated users to Deactivate
questions.answer: Set the AD option for deactivated users to Deactivate
questions.explanation: The directory's To Okta lifecycle setting decides what Okta does when the source account is disabled. Deactivate Users under To App acts in the other direction.

questions.stem: Users are mastered by an HR app. HR records a termination. What deactivates the user in Okta?
choices: The Deactivate Users feature in each downstream app
A manual password expiry by the help desk
The HR app's lifecycle sourcing at the next import
A sign-in attempt that fails the session policy
questions.answer: The HR app's lifecycle sourcing at the next import
questions.explanation: When the HR app is a profile source, a termination there changes the user's Okta status at import. Downstream app features act only after Okta's status changes.

questions.stem: AD accounts are sometimes disabled briefly during investigations. The admin wants Okta to block these users while keeping their app assignments. Which option fits?
choices: Set the AD option for deactivated users to Suspend
Set the AD option for deactivated users to Deactivate
Set the AD option for deactivated users to Do nothing
Remove the AD option and expire passwords manually
questions.answer: Set the AD option for deactivated users to Suspend
questions.explanation: Suspending blocks sign-in but leaves assignments untouched, ideal for temporary disablement. Deactivate would remove all assignments.

questions.stem: A user disabled in Active Directory two days ago is still Active in Okta, although imports run every hour. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The AD option for deactivated users is set to Do nothing
The user's Okta password has not been expired
The user is not enrolled in Okta FastPass
The AD app is missing an attribute statement
questions.answer: The AD option for deactivated users is set to Do nothing
questions.explanation: With Do nothing, a disabled source account leaves the Okta user unchanged. Authenticators and attribute statements do not drive lifecycle from AD.

questions.stem: Okta should restore access automatically when a previously disabled AD account is enabled again. Which setting should the admin configure?
choices: The Create Users feature under To App on the AD integration's Provisioning tab
A global session policy rule for reactivated AD users
The AD option to reactivate users when they are reactivated in AD
The Sync Password feature for the AD integration
questions.answer: The AD option to reactivate users when they are reactivated in AD
questions.explanation: The To Okta lifecycle settings can reactivate Okta users when the source account is enabled. Create Users makes accounts in a target app, not in Okta.

questions.stem: Accounts with no sign-in for 90 days should be suspended automatically in Okta. What should the admin set up?
choices: A password policy with a 90-day maximum password age
An automation with a user inactivity condition and a lifecycle action
A global session policy rule with a maximum session lifetime of 90 days
A group rule that removes inactive users from Everyone
questions.answer: An automation with a user inactivity condition and a lifecycle action
questions.explanation: Okta Automations can act on user inactivity and change the user's lifecycle state. Password age only forces a password change.

questions.stem: Put the steps of offboarding a terminated employee in order.
items: Review the user's Applications tab for apps without provisioning
Disable the accounts in apps that Okta does not provision
Attempt a sign-in as the user to Okta and those apps
Confirm the deactivation and the failed sign-in attempts in the System Log
questions.explanation: Assignments disappear on deactivation, so the app list is reviewed first. Then the user is deactivated, leftover accounts are disabled, a test sign-in is attempted and the System Log confirms the results.

questions.stem: Match each user status to the situation that causes it.

pairs.match: Admin blocked sign-in but kept assignments
Admin removed access and app assignments

targets_extra: User changed their own display name
questions.explanation: Each status reflects a lifecycle step or admin action. A profile change by the user does not alter account status.

questions.stem: Which TWO results occur when an admin deactivates an Active user?
choices: All of the user's app assignments are removed
The user's password is permanently deleted
The user's profile is permanently deleted from Okta
The user is moved back to Staged status
The user's app assignments are kept for later
answers: All of the user's app assignments are removed
The user's password is permanently deleted
questions.explanation: Deactivation removes app assignments and the password but keeps the profile until the user is deleted. Keeping assignments describes suspension.
